result.question: If a component has MTTF of one million hours, what failure rate follows from the slides' reciprocal relationship, in failures per hour and FIT?

retrieved_chunks.text: FAILURE RATE In Computer Architecture, failure rate tells us how frequently a component is expected to fail. The simplest relationship with MTTF is: λ= 1/MTTF The reciprocal of MTTF is a rate of failures, generally reported as failures per billion hours of operation,or FIT(for failures in time).

EXAMPLE • Assume a disk subsystem with the following components and MTTF: • 10 disks, each rated at 1,000,000-hour MTTF • 1 ATA controller, 500,000-hour MTTF • 1 power supply, 200,000-hour MTTF • 1 fan, 200,000-hour MTTF • 1 ATA cable, 1,000,000-hour MTTF Compute the MTTF of the system as a whole.

DEPENDABILITY • Transitions between these two states are caused by failures (from state 1 to state 2) or restorations (2 to 1). Quantifying these transitions leads to the two main measures of dependability: • Module reliability is a measure of the continuous service accomplishment (or, equivalently, of the time to failure) from a reference initial instant. Therefore the mean time to failure (MTTF) is a reliability measure.

DEPENDABILITY • Historically,integrated circuits were one of the most reliable components of a computer. Although their pins may be vulnerable, and faults may occur over communication channels, the failure rate inside the chip was very low.

EXERCISE A computer system contains a critical memory module.It fails on average every 1500 hours of operation and takes 6 hours to repair.After a redesign, its MTTF increases to 1800 hours, but because the new design is more complicated, MTTR increases to 12 hours. Calculate the original MTBF. Calculate original availability. Calculate redesigned MTBF. Calculate redesigned availability. Did the redesign improve availability?
